name: ScriptaHub – Create book
description: Process one reserved book in sequential editorial steps, translate accepted resources when requested, validate the package and publish.

tasks.name: Read the selected book request
tasks.prompt:
Follow scriptahub-tasks SKILL.md and the operation reference for execution context, native calls, recovery, handoff, source scope and acceptance.

Read exactly the one request supplied by the parent dispatcher. Do not call batch-start, batch-next, batch-close or claim, create execution/run IDs, select another request or launch child workflows. This child uses the same flow root and tasks/<taskId> directory as its parent.

Use the parent-created handoff. Read taskDirectory/run-state/claimed.json and the existing taskDirectory/run-state/handoff.json once. Accept step=select-task as the parent-created initial context. Do not create a replacement if a resumed execution has lost its handoff. Verify taskId, executionId, runId and bookId against the parent objective. Preserve existing context, pinned editorialSource, accepted editorialResults, native jobs and publication evidence. Check this execution's service status once. A missing/mismatched identity is a real error: invoke the runtime report-task-blocked skill with that exact cause, not a route to publication.

Save processingMode in the handoff: terminal for an already completed/failed/cancelled execution; publication-recovery for publicationPending=true; cancel for stop_requested before pending publication; process otherwise. Also retain actual serviceState, task values, processingSettings, configured repositories, taskDirectory and evidence paths. Never invent source files, validation approval or publication receipts.

Use scriptahub-tasks handoff with step=resume-book, directory=taskDirectory and the preserved context. Complete this step and pass only the durable handoff path and actual mode to Prepare or generate the book. There is one outgoing edge. Do not jump to publishing or the result. Downstream preparation/editorial/package/validation steps read processingMode first: for terminal, publication-recovery or cancel they pass the existing context unchanged and perform no content work or repeated checks. Publish the book alone reconciles the registered publication or acknowledges cancellation; terminal mode only reports the saved result. This straight path never regenerates a book or manufactures approvals for recovery.

tasks.name: Prepare or generate the book
tasks.prompt:
Follow scriptahub-tasks SKILL.md and the operation reference for execution context, native calls, recovery, handoff, source scope and acceptance.

Read the task and processingSettings provided by the parent and resume-book. Do not claim another task or create a new runId. If the service now shows a non-running state in process mode, stop and report the actual status to the parent through report-task-blocked; do not generate content or jump to publication. The parent batch helper already performed preflight and publication checks. This child never claims or traverses the batch. If editorialSource is already pinned, verify its path and SHA-256, and verify every saved manuscript edition and PDF reference against its stored hashes. Forward the saved source profile and handoff. Otherwise choose the path using the service-provided task.type and files. Files with role=cover are cover artwork, never manuscripts. If present, download the cover through the helper into <taskDirectory>/sources/cover.<actual extension>, verify its SHA-256 and record coverSourcePath and coverSourceHash separately in the handoff. Exclude cover artwork from manuscript sourceHashes and all content conversion.

For scriptahub.manuscript, require at least one uploaded manuscript file with role other than cover. Download those documents through the helper and verify their hashes. Preserve the original bytes. With multiple documents, work in separate sources/manuscripts/<file-index>/ directories, and determine each language from substantial manuscript text, using declared language as supporting evidence rather than guessing from the filename or UI. Use doc2pdf only for DOC/DOCX. Keep an existing PDF unchanged. Run PDF integrity checks and pdf2html conversion with the prepared runtime. Reuse the converted HTML used for detection.

Follow explicit instructions that select or combine source documents, restrict edition languages, or ask to translate from a particular source. Otherwise, when different manuscript languages are detected, create one edition of the same book per detected language directly from its corresponding manuscript. A requested language with an available manuscript uses that manuscript unless the user explicitly asks for a fresh translation. When building multiple direct editions, if there is more than one plausible manuscript for a language and the instructions do not resolve the choice, report the ambiguous files rather than silently dropping or merging them. Use canonical BCP 47 language tags. Choose the primary edition from an explicitly designated original or, otherwise, the first selected manuscript in upload order. Preserve the title of each edition (apply explicit title instructions when supplied). Set each converted HTML document’s lang to the detected edition language before hashing it. Before editorial processing, pin manuscriptEditions keyed by language with entries {path,sha256,language,title,referencePdf,referencePdfSha256}. Include all direct editions, including the primary, when more than one is selected. Set editorialSource to {path,sha256,language} from the primary edition and record its actual sourceLanguage and referencePdf. Reuse the complete map on resume.

For scriptahub.book-proposal, require no manuscript files (files with role other than cover). An optional cover image does not change this path. Never ask for a manuscript or use the cover as book content; download only the optional cover as described above. Use task.values.description as the book's subject or story brief. Read the structured instructions audience, purpose, scope, structure, viewpoints and qualityCriteria from task.values. Use only the nonempty fields as editorial requirements. When no meaningful description exists, report that exact error through report-task-blocked and stop the child. Use the requested book language when explicit, otherwise task.language, otherwise the brief language; default to English only if undetermined.

Create a private brief at <taskDirectory>/run-state/generation-brief.md. Compose it with this objective: "Write a complete original book in the specified language, based on the subject and editorial instructions below. Deliver full chapters with complete prose." Include the book language, description, nonempty instructions by field and the final book title. Use the first nonblank value from task.values.titles or task.values.title as supplied, trimming outer whitespace. If both are blank, use the brief to choose a single, specific title in the primary book language. Aim for 3–8 words and match the intended audience, tone, genre and requested style. Treat these as editorial inputs under the shared execution contract. Use the current RoboTeam model to draft the full manuscript in coherent chapters with the intended audience, scope, structure, perspectives and quality criteria. Use verifiable sources for factual claims and do not invent citations, quotations, credentials or attributed experiences. Use reasonable editorial defaults for unspecified options. Keep the brief out of the publication package.

Write the generated source as self-contained semantic HTML at <taskDirectory>/sources/generated.html with a correct html lang, title, and main[data-reader-content]. Use semantic headings, paragraphs and tables; no scripts, remote assets or copied placeholder content. For a book proposal, use the final title in the HTML <title> and the book-title heading. Save the title as bookTitle in the durable handoff with the pinned source. On resume, reuse the saved title or recover it from the completed source HTML <title> if the handoff lacks it. Author the book once; reuse an already completed manuscript for the same task when resuming. Keep the publication and its generated sources in HTML. Pin this HTML as the authored source. Record sourceKind=generated, sourceHashes=[] and referencePdf=null. Keep the private brief out of the package. Record an uploaded manuscript PDF as the source reference when present.

Save the full HTML, source profile and applicable technical-check evidence in the handoff. Independent book acceptance follows package preparation. Reuse matching successful checks; report a concrete preparation failure through report-task-blocked.

For scriptahub.fork use the generated HTML output path. First use the download helper for task.files[0] to retrieve the verified full source edition into a private sources path. Read that content as editorial source material. Write a complete distinct book under the requested title and apply task.values.prompt. Record task.source verbatim for attribution. Include an attribution and a note about modifications in the book. Keep the downloaded source file and generation brief out of the public package. Process this task as a generated book for all subsequent steps.

Multilingual generation request: honor an explicitly named original/source language first; otherwise, for an explicit list of book languages choose English when it is listed, or the first requested language when it is not. Do not let UI language override that explicit multilingual request. For an uploaded manuscript retain its actual source language. Record the original requirement evidence and canonical requested language list in the handoff; do not generate separate original books per language.

Pin the final full book HTML in editorialSource={path,sha256,language} in the durable handoff. Reuse the pinned bytes on resume. Pass that handoff to the comprehensive summary.

tasks.name: Create the comprehensive summary
tasks.prompt:
Follow scriptahub-tasks SKILL.md and the operation reference for execution context, native calls, recovery, handoff, source scope and acceptance.

Apply processingMode from the handoff. In process mode verify the pinned editorial source and check the service status. Work through this stage in order. Resume the first unfinished artifact and preserve matching accepted results. Pass the durable handoff through the single outgoing edge.

Prepare the pinned source with comprehensive-summary at <taskDirectory>/editorial-jobs/comprehensive-summary using --minutes 10 --max-duration and --output <taskDirectory>/editorial/comprehensive-summary.html. Treat the server's 10 minutes as a ceiling for every edition. Use the job’s returned target as guidance and write a shorter summary when appropriate to the source. Complete native batch analysis, synthesis and draft in order, then build and independently validate against the pinned source. Save the successful receipt and editorialResults entry using step=comprehensive-summary.

tasks.name: Extract relevant keywords
tasks.prompt:
Follow scriptahub-tasks SKILL.md and the operation reference for execution context, native calls, recovery, handoff, source scope and acceptance.

Apply processingMode from the handoff. In process mode verify the pinned editorial source and check the service status. Work through this stage in order. Resume the first unfinished artifact and preserve matching accepted results. Pass the durable handoff through the single outgoing edge.

Use relevant-keywords analyze on editorialSource.path with --count 20 and --job-dir <taskDirectory>/editorial-jobs/relevant-keywords. Complete the analyses and selection.json, then build. Use the returned relevantKeywords.txt path beside the source and retain the successful build as evidence. Save the editorialResults entry using step=relevant-keywords.

tasks.name: Analyze the book for presentation and description
tasks.prompt:
Follow scriptahub-tasks SKILL.md and the operation reference for execution context, native calls, recovery, handoff, source scope and acceptance.

Apply processingMode from the handoff. In process mode verify the pinned editorial source and check the service status. Work through this stage in order. Resume the first unfinished artifact and preserve matching accepted results. Pass the durable handoff through the single outgoing edge.

Use the shared-editorial operation in scriptahub-tasks. If no shared job exists and both final outputs are already accepted with matching receipts, forward the handoff. Otherwise prepare or resume the native jobs at <taskDirectory>/editorial-jobs/shared/marketing-summary and <taskDirectory>/editorial-jobs/shared/short-description. Use editorialSource.path and the same canonical BCP 47 language from the handoff for both. Set --output to <taskDirectory>/editorial/marketing-summary.html and <taskDirectory>/editorial/short-description.html respectively. Pass --shared-editorial to both prepare commands so they use the same reader-content root and source units.

Use action=status to get the missing batches. For each missing batch sequentially, request action=contract, read the indicated batch once, and submit one analysis using action=submit, the returned batchSha256, and the exact shared schema. Capture safe hooks and neutral themes from the same reading and identify protected revelations once for both resources. The operation saves each accepted batch to <taskDirectory>/editorial/shared-analysis.json. When status is complete save its evidence (path and SHA-256) as sharedEditorialAnalysis in the handoff using step=shared-editorial-analysis.

tasks.name: Write and validate the book presentation
tasks.prompt:
Follow scriptahub-tasks SKILL.md and the operation reference for execution context, native calls, recovery, handoff, source scope and acceptance.

Apply processingMode from the handoff. In process mode verify the pinned editorial source and check the service status. Work through this stage in order. Resume the first unfinished artifact and preserve matching accepted results. Pass the durable handoff through the single outgoing edge.

Use the shared editorial synchronization and correction procedure for role=marketing-summary. If the output is already accepted against matching evidence, forward it. Persist any pending sharedEditorialAnalysis update before projecting batches. From those accepted analyses create the synthesis, draft and independent spoiler review as required by native status. Build the presentation and validate it independently against editorialSource.path. Save the successful receipt and current projectionSha256 in this role’s editorialResults entry using step=marketing-summary.

tasks.name: Write and validate the short description
tasks.prompt:
Follow scriptahub-tasks SKILL.md and the operation reference for execution context, native calls, recovery, handoff, source scope and acceptance.

Apply processingMode from the handoff. In process mode verify the pinned editorial source and check the service status. Work through this stage in order. Resume the first unfinished artifact and preserve matching accepted results. Pass the durable handoff through the single outgoing edge.

Use the shared editorial synchronization and correction procedure for role=short-description. If the output is already accepted against matching evidence, forward it. Persist any pending sharedEditorialAnalysis update before projecting batches. Draft the 4–6 sourced thematic sentences and independently review them against the accepted evidence and protected revelations. Build and independently validate against editorialSource.path. Save the successful receipt and current projectionSha256 in this role’s editorialResults entry using step=short-description.

tasks.name: Verify editorial outputs and select destination
tasks.prompt:
Follow scriptahub-tasks SKILL.md and the operation reference for execution context, native calls, recovery, handoff, source scope and acceptance.

Apply processingMode from the handoff. In process mode verify the pinned source. If sharedEditorialAnalysis exists, run shared-editorial status. Apply the shared editorial procedure only to affected roles, in presentation then description order, and require shared-editorial verify to pass before routing. Verify all four editorialResults entries against their output bytes and successful receipts. Save the assembled handoff using step=process-content.

Conditional translation decision: derive targets only from the original explicit user requirement and the pinned source language. Canonicalize tags with Intl.Locale, remove duplicates and every language already covered by a direct manuscript edition, and save translationRequest={explicit,targets,evidence}. The translation input manifest uses the primary manuscript and its accepted editorial resources from manuscriptEditorial[primaryLanguage] when present. If direct manuscript editions cover the whole request, route to package preparation. Empty targets route through editorial-to-package. Explicit nonempty targets require the manifest below and route through editorial-to-translations. Report a requested translation with unresolved target languages as a concrete missing requirement.

Only when explicit=true and targets is nonempty, write a compact translation input manifest at <taskDirectory>/editorial/translation-inputs.json. It names this execution/book/source language, canonical target languages and the existing validated full book HTML, comprehensive summary HTML, marketing summary HTML, short-description HTML, keywords text and available reader-facing book metadata. For each resource record its stable resource ID, actual source path, SHA-256, format and successful validation evidence. Include all four editorial outputs; do not regenerate them or translate them here. For a book proposal use handoff.bookTitle as the original reader-facing title. Reference the manifest path in the handoff and take editorial-to-translations.

After all required results pass, select a publication destination from task.repositories using the pinned book and actual catalogue metadata. Reuse an existing recorded destination. For multiple suitable destinations use scriptahub-tasks choose without clarification. Resolve the actual branch/content root using the configured URL and Git references, never guess main/master. Preserve numeric schema 1 or 2; only a confirmed entirely empty repository may initialize schema 2. Record the configured catalogue, branch, content root, baseCommit (or null for an empty repository) and concise reasoning. The coordinator only assembles result paths/receipts and the destination in the handoff. Complete the editorial step once the four editorial results and destination are ready, then use exactly the applicable translation condition above. Report a real unrecoverable editorial error or no suitable destination through report-task-blocked with the precise cause.

# nextNodePrompt
Handoff path, actual operation outcome and at most five unresolved findings (maximum 1,200 characters). Select editorial-to-translations only for explicit nonempty translation targets; otherwise select editorial-to-package.

# nextEdgeId
editorial-to-translations when translationRequest.explicit=true and translationRequest.targets is nonempty; otherwise editorial-to-package.

tasks.name: Translate resources — only if requested
tasks.prompt:
Follow scriptahub-tasks SKILL.md and the operation reference for execution context, native calls, recovery, handoff, source scope and acceptance.

Translation is authorized ONLY by translationRequest.explicit=true with a nonempty canonical targets list traced to the original user requirement. Read the existing handoff and translation-inputs.json once; verify execution/book identity, requested targets, source hashes and validation evidence against the accepted originals. An unauthorized visit performs no work and forwards the unchanged handoff to package preparation. Apply the processingMode forwarding rules from scriptahub-tasks. Never infer extra languages or generate a PDF/DOCX for translation.

This step receives the WHOLE accepted resource set: full book HTML, comprehensive summary HTML, marketing summary HTML, short-description HTML, keywords text and existing reader-facing metadata. For every explicitly requested target language, translate each existing resource from its OWN source. Do not regenerate a summary, description or keywords from a translated book; do not use a summary instead of the full book. Do not chain target languages. Keep source artifacts byte-for-byte unchanged. Translate reader-facing title, descriptions and alt/title/accessibility text; preserve identifiers, URLs, file hashes, citations, non-reader technical values and provenance. Record missing optional metadata as absent instead of inventing it. All four editorial outputs and full-book content are required.

Use native translate-html prepare/build/validate for each HTML resource, with distinct resumable job directories under <taskDirectory>/translation-jobs/<target>/<resource-id> and outputs under <taskDirectory>/translations/<target>/. Read the actual CLI contract for supported flags, bootstrap review and batch schemas. Use the accepted HTML as translation input. If an original PDF manuscript exists, keep it unchanged as the original reference and translate its already verified HTML representation.

Adapt UTF-8 keywords to the native HTML translator as follows. Create a separate minimal semantic HTML adapter that XML-escapes the original keyword strings, uses one stable element per keyword and retains the original list order. Reader-facing text metadata may use the same approach with stable field markers. Preserve and hash the adapters as exact translation sources; never modify the originals. Translate and natively validate the adapters, then extract only their identified translated text fields into target keywords/metadata. Preserve keyword count/order/concepts and metadata keys/technical values, with a semantic terminology check; do not regenerate, add concepts, summarize or replace the original outputs. Keep adapters/job reports private rather than publishing them as book content.

Derive a consistent per-target glossary from the source book and reviewed terminology across all resources. Freeze that context, complete the native bootstrap review and assign independent targets/resources to the available workers under the shared concurrency/admission contract.

Reuse translations only when resource source hash, target language, effective parameters, accepted output hash and successful validation evidence still match. Resume the first incomplete/invalid native batch rather than replacing accepted outputs or rerunning preparation over matching jobs. Correct only concrete findings. Store successful native responses under <taskDirectory>/translations/receipts/<target>-<resource-id>.json outside temporary jobs. Write <taskDirectory>/translations/manifest.json recording each source resource ID/path/hash, target language, target resource path/hash, native job and validation receipt, plus metadata/keyword extraction evidence. Every target must have an explicit outcome: complete only when its whole resource set passed, otherwise failed or not_attempted with an actual concise reason. Verify no source bytes changed. Exclude an incomplete target edition rather than blocking publication of the validated source and other complete targets. Never label an incomplete target complete.

Save only translation manifest/glossary/receipt paths, actual targets and status in the preserved durable handoff using step=translate-resources. Forward those paths to package preparation through the single outgoing edge. Do not create a cover, choose another request, grant credits, publish or call finish here.

# nextNodePrompt
Durable handoff path, translation manifest path, actual targets and validation outcome; no route selection is needed.

Finish the ledger even when every target failed. Set publicationLanguages to all direct manuscript editions (or the source language for a single source) plus complete targets. Include all direct editions in translationOutcome.requestedLanguages and publishedLanguages and save the outcome in the handoff using the shared contract. Retain each omitted language and actual reason, then forward to package preparation.

tasks.name: Prepare the publication package and cover
tasks.prompt:
Follow scriptahub-tasks SKILL.md and the operation reference for execution context, native calls, recovery, handoff, source scope and acceptance.

In process mode, assemble <taskDirectory>/package at the pinned destination. Use every direct manuscript edition and its own accepted editorial assets, plus complete target language resource sets from the translation ledger. If there is no translation ledger, stage all direct editions. For each direct manuscript edition use its own reader, title, keywords and PDF reference. Keep omitted targets out of the package and preserve their recorded reasons. Apply the shared package preparation and schema 1 keyword index procedure. Retain verified manuscript resources, package only this book and preserve the configured schema. For a fork record task.source verbatim in provenance.fork and keep the downloaded baseline private.

Stage the full reader and accepted comprehensive summary as distinct resources for every included language. In schema 1 use <language>/full_content.html and <language>/comprehensive-summary.html inside the book directory; point the edition history source filename at the full reader. In schema 2 stage them under the book directory. Leave reading-route mappings and the landing page to prepare-reading-routes. Carry the accepted short description and marketing presentation paragraphs. For a book proposal use handoff.bookTitle for the original-language title in the catalogue, book metadata and generated cover. Use the accepted localized title for each translated edition.

Resolve genuine package defects here before freezing the inventory. For each direct manuscript edition, use its verified PDF for source fidelity. Restrict any native preparation corrections to the corresponding staged reader and concrete findings. Use complete only with its supported declared-source layout, or audit-only prepare with explicit inputs. Keep accepted sources, translations and editorial files intact.

For coverMode=upload, use the verified PNG/JPG/WebP unchanged for every included language. Preserve the upload SHA-256 and use the same file for cover and thumbnail. For a generated cover, combine the actual final title, book subject and coverStyle, coverPalette, coverComposition and coverDescription into a private review/cover-brief.json. Create a self-contained portrait SVG with viewBox 0 0 1200 1800, legible title and static local content. Reuse the illustration; use the accepted local title for each included edition. Reuse a verified cover on retry. Stage the cover and thumbnail files for each included language.

For a generated book or fork, write <taskDirectory>/review/edition-plan.json with editions=[{language,baselineHtml,baselineSha256,candidateHtml,changesPath,changesSha256}] for every included reader. Use the immutable authored source or accepted translated HTML as its baseline, the staged full reader as candidate and an empty changes array. Paths are relative to the flow root.

Before hashing the inventory for a generated book or fork, run native validate-book compare-edition for each planned baseline and staged reader with its empty change plan. Save the preparation reports in <taskDirectory>/review/layout-LANGUAGE. The command checks standalone HTML and the imported reader at 1440, 1024 and 390 CSS pixels. Read both new and existing findings; both counts must be zero in the staged reader. For a reported wide table, adjust only the staged table presentation so columns fit and cell text wraps at 390 px. Preserve the table structure, captions, content and pinned baseline; avoid hiding or clipping cells. For standalone-only findings, use responsive CSS in the staged HTML. For imported-reader findings, apply any candidate-specific presentation to the table or its cells using inline styles, which survive import. Rerun the audit for changed candidates and report any remaining concrete blocker during preparation. Save the passing preparation report paths in the handoff.

After the layout checks, call scriptahub-tasks prepare-reading-routes with the collection path and staged editions. Pass each staged cover and optional thumbnail as cover and thumbnail paths relative to the book directory. The helper writes the reader and artwork mappings, localized descriptions, and schema 2 checksums before inventory hashing. Use its returned reader paths for the edition plan. Freeze the package, verify its draft inventory with checkReadingRoutes=true and save step=review-correct with package, inventory, edition plan and cover evidence paths. The final acceptance step takes these exact bytes.

tasks.name: Validate the publication package
tasks.prompt:
Follow scriptahub-tasks SKILL.md and the operation reference for execution context, native calls, recovery, handoff, source scope and acceptance.

In process mode, independently validate the frozen package. For a generated book or fork, run native compare-edition for every language in the edition plan against its pinned authored or accepted translated baseline. Use changes=[] and a separate validation directory per language. Require zero errors and zero existing findings. For an uploaded manuscript, run fresh audit-only validate-book prepare for each direct edition against its staged HTML and its own verified PDF. Save native manuscript evidence in separate <taskDirectory>/validation/source-layout/<language> directories. Use --pdf and --english to select those exact files as needed; --english names the reference HTML argument for the auditor, regardless of the book's locale. Use --languages en to audit only the reference when translations are already independently validated by their translator.

Verify each included language has complete accepted reader and editorial resources. Final package verification enforces distinct View Book, Read Online and Read in 10 Min routes and the comprehensive-summary mapping. When translations were requested, reconcile the accepted resources and validation receipts with publicationLanguages and the omission ledger. Keep omitted targets out of the package. Pass the actual translationOutcome to final verification.

Verify that each new language maps its cover and thumbnail to inventoried, readable local bytes. For uploaded art compare to coverSourceHash. For generated art check the portrait SVG, title and the private cover brief. Reject scripts, foreignObject, event handlers, animation and external or data references; inspect rendered cover and thumbnail if the available browser can render them and record what was checked.

Run verify-package with finalize=true and the prepared draft inventory. For generated books pass editionPlan and audits=[{language,report}], one native report per published language. For multiple direct manuscript editions pass audits=[{language,report}], one native report per pinned manuscript edition. For a single manuscript pass audit, sourceLanguage and referencePdf. Include the exact package root, destination and book/execution identity. Save only the helper's approval paths in step=validate-final. Report missing or failed required evidence with its actual cause. This step leaves package bytes untouched.

tasks.name: Publish the book
tasks.prompt:
Follow scriptahub-tasks SKILL.md and the operation reference for execution context, native calls, recovery, handoff, source scope and acceptance.

Use the shared publication procedure with the actual service status and the approval saved by validate-final. Preserve translationOutcome in the exact final validation delivered to the service. Save the actual response and receipt in step=publish-result. Forward the confirmed result or concrete blocker to the single-book summary and parent reconciliation.

tasks.name: Summarize this book result
tasks.prompt:
Follow scriptahub-tasks SKILL.md and the operation reference for execution context, native calls, recovery, handoff, source scope and acceptance.

Read this request's durable handoff and saved publication-result only. Summarize the single book's actual state, title, published repository/commit when confirmed, or precise failure/cancellation cause. Preserve all artifacts. Do not reserve, claim, settle or select another task, start workflows, regenerate outputs, publish or call finish here. This is the end of the child flow. Return a concise technical payload outside the human report with taskDirectory, executionId, actual terminal state and handoff/publication receipt paths so the parent can confirm the service state. Do not label a pending/uncertain publication as completed; report the actual blocker and retain the same execution for reconciliation.

When source publication succeeded but translationOutcome.omitted is nonempty, report the request as partially completed: name the actual published languages and list each omitted language with its real reason (failed or not attempted). Read the confirmed task result/receipt and actual language ledger, not only a successful graph status. Report the source publication and omitted targets with their actual distinct outcomes. The ScriptaHub task result and completion notification must carry the same warning.

defaultObjective: Resume and complete only the existing book request identified by the parent objective, using its taskDirectory, claimed identity and handoff. Do not claim or traverse any batch.
